task_instance: Given a stakeholder's raw feature request for a 'Notification Center', break it into an epic of INVEST-validated user stories with Given-When-Then acceptance criteria and Fibonacci story points (per the skill's Epic Breakdown / User Story Generation workflows), score the backlog with the skill's weighted prioritization formula (value 40%/impact 30%/risk 15%/effort 15%), and produce a Sprint 1 plan using the skill's capacity formula (velocity x availability factor, 85% committed / 15% stretch).
blocker_detail: Not a blocker for the core deliverable, but noted: the skill's Tools section references `scripts/user_story_generator.py` and `references/user-story-templates.md` / `references/sprint-planning-guide.md`, none of which exist in the skill's source directory (only SKILL.md and LICENSE are present). Per the additional rules, that bundled script/reference set was not run or reimplemented; instead the core deliverable (stories, AC, INVEST validation, prioritization, sprint plan) was produced directly from the fully-specified templates and formulas already embedded in SKILL.md, which is what a user invoking this skill actually wants.
evidence: Created sample_epic_input.md (a realistic raw stakeholder request). Wrote user_stories.md: 7 user stories (US-001..US-007) breaking down the 'Notification Center' epic, each with type/priority/points, a full As-a/I-want/So-that story, Given-When-Then + Should/Must acceptance criteria (counts matched to the skill's Minimum Criteria by Story Size table), an explicit INVEST 6-point checklist per story, and a dependency-aware sequencing section, all following the skill's Epic Breakdown Workflow and Splitting Techniques verbatim. Wrote backlog_prioritization.py implementing the skill's exact weighted formula (0.40/0.30/0.15/0.15) over the 7 stories; ran it (`python3 backlog_prioritization.py`, output captured in backlog_prioritization_output.txt) producing a ranked score table (e.g. US-002 4.30, US-007 4.25, ... US-006 2.60). Wrote capacity_calc.py implementing the skill's 'Sprint Capacity = Average Velocity x Availability Factor' formula plus 85%/15% commit/stretch split; ran it (capacity_calc_output.txt) giving Average velocity 28.0, factor 0.9, capacity 25.2, committed 21.4, stretch 3.8. Wrote sprint_plan.md assembling a concrete Sprint 1 (committed: US-007, US-001, US-002, US-003, US-004 = 19 pts, within the 21.4-pt 85% ceiling; US-005/US-006 carried to Sprint 2 due to size vs remaining stretch budget and dependency ordering), with an explicit validation section confirming committed points <= 85% capacity and that every committed story has both acceptance criteria and a passed INVEST check. Verified by inspection of all script outputs and by cross-checking every story/AC/score against the specific tables and formulas in SKILL.md (User Story Template, GWT Template, Minimum Criteria by Story Size, Splitting Techniques, Capacity Calculation, Availability Factors, Prioritization Factors, INVEST Criteria). Files produced (all under the work directory): sample_epic_input.md, user_stories.md, backlog_prioritization.py, backlog_prioritization_output.txt, capacity_calc.py, capacity_calc_output.txt, sprint_plan.md, result.json.
